notes: Iteration 2 reruns only the with-skill configuration (rubric 0.1.1, opaque fixture ids, neutral input paths, evals outside the skill). The without-skill outputs are copied from iteration 1 to save usage after two rate-limit stops; they saw the iteration-1 bundles.

Offline scorer vs developer annotations: frozen-skill TP 12, FP 0, FN 0 (P = R = F1 = 1.0), zero evidence-validity errors. CAUTION: the reference was revised after iteration 1 (LAY-01 item added; LAY-02/DAT-04 rule clarified in the codebook), so this is tuning-set performance on six synthetic pages, not evidence of accuracy. Held-out data and independent annotators are required before any claim.

The specific iteration-1 problems went away for the stated reasons: the template page now uses DAT-04 primary with LAY-02 secondary (0.1.1 rule); the injection audit marks DAT-01 unassessed and status partial instead of 'assessed' while abstaining; captions and fine print map to their own regions after the capture fix.

Slop-association agreement with the developer fell to 33% exact (100% within one level): the auditor rated several template-page findings 'strong' where the developer used 'moderate'. The anchors may need clearer guidance on when several correlated cues justify 'strong'; this is a human-piloting question, not something to tune on six fixtures.
Cost: the template-page run took about 9.6 minutes and 219k tokens (38 tool calls, including pixel decoding in pure Python); other runs took 4 to 5 minutes and 145k to 178k tokens.
New finding by the auditors, not planted: the scenario fixture's bars do not render at mobile width (a CSS defect in the fixture). Both iterations recorded it as a quality observation, not slop.
